idiom_name: hand-written in-memory implementation of the collaborator interface with a typed operation journal
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: implement the collaborator's operations for real over an in-memory store, append a typed, domain-level record of each received operation to an ordered journal, and expose the journal only to tests through accessors that are not part of the production interface. Nothing in a language's standard library replaces this compound, because the journal entries are domain operations; mocking libraries record calls but do not implement working behaviour, so they cover the spy and mock rows instead. Install the fake through the existing substitutable dependency, re-create or clear it per test, keep it a faithful subset of the real collaborator's contract (validate it with a shared contract test), and assert selectively - filtered by operation, ordered only where order is contractual.
pitfalls: Asserting the whole journal, including incidental operations and their order, overspecifies the system under test's algorithm and breaks on behaviour-preserving refactorings.
Sharing one journaling fake across tests (static or module-level state, a shared fixture) leaks recorded history and makes failures order-dependent.
Letting the fake be more permissive than the real collaborator - ignoring validation, uniqueness or error paths - produces green tests for sequences production would reject.
